newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: FOREIGNERS CUT NET S.AFRICA BOND BUYS BY A THIRD.
newsitem.headline: FOREIGNERS CUT NET S.AFRICA BOND BUYS BY A THIRD.

text.p: Foreigners have sold just under one billion rand's worth of South African gilts over the last two days, reducing their net purchases so far this year by nearly a third.
Figures released by the Bond Exchange of South Africa show foreigners sold 471.79 rand worth of gilts on Wednesday after selling 476.21 million rand on Tuesday.
This brings total net purchases to 2.24 billion rand from the 3.188 billion rand bought by the close of trade on Monday.
Analysts said the foreign selling stemmed primarily from the rand's renewed gyrations.
The bond market has been shaken this week by the rand's slide to new lows against the dollar with the yield on the key R150 stock rising to a five-month high of 16.09 percent early on Thursday.
The rand fell to an all-time low of 4.7670 bid against the dollar early on Thursday.
The gilt sales come, however, at a time when there is increased foreign participation on the local bond market.
Foreign turnover on the Bond Exchange is expected to total between 31 billion and 32 billion rand in October, according to analysts, compared with the 11.9 billion rand recorded in January this year.
